title: Backpressure: Four Policies, One Overload
summary: Block, drop-new, drop-old, and circuit breaker, run against the same producer that outruns its consumer — including proof that drop-new and drop-old discard the same number of items, but never the same ones.

title: Cache Freshness: What Stale-While-Revalidate Actually Buys You
summary: Three real cache-freshness policies run against the same origin outage — TTL-blocking errors, stale-while-revalidate never blocks at all, and stale-if-error sits in between, paying for a synchronous origin attempt even when it ends up serving the same stale content SWR would have served for free.

title: Canary Deploys and the Sample Size Nobody Checks
summary: A real two-proportion z-test canary analysis, run stage by stage — proving that the same real regression can go completely undetected at a small sample size and get caught at a larger one, using the exact statistic, not a story about it.

title: Distributed Locks: Redlock and the Pause That Breaks It
summary: Run the real Redlock quorum algorithm against nodes you crash yourself, then simulate the exact pause Martin Kleppmann's 2016 critique is about — and see why Antirez's own rebuttal doesn't actually disagree with it.

title: gRPC vs REST: When the Smaller Payload Loses
summary: A real harness measuring gRPC against REST for the same data, same server, same Go process — and REST wins throughput at every concurrency level tested for a small payload, and at half the concurrency levels tested for a 100x larger one.

title: Leader Election: Running the Actual Bully Algorithm, Not a Diagram of It
summary: Crash the leader and watch the real Bully algorithm elect a new one, message by message — including the O(n^2) worst case the protocol is criticized for.

title: Connection Pooling: When PgBouncer Actually Helps
summary: A real harness measuring PgBouncer against direct Postgres across two connection lifecycles — the advantage widens under one and reverses under the other, so 'add a pooler' isn't a universal answer.

title: Field Note: What My Own Git Log Proves About Spec-Driven Development
summary: PFM's governance docs claim every business rule traces from spec to test to code. A plain git log, not the docs, is what actually proves it — and it also shows two honest cases of deliberately not fixing something.

title: The Hidden Costs of Firebase Cloud Functions
summary: A follow-up to the field note on choosing Firebase Functions over Cloud Run: two costs the concurrency model doesn't advertise on its own.

title: ADR: Tracing vs Metrics for Observability in Aegis
summary: An Architecture Decision Record on why distributed tracing and metrics answer different questions in Aegis, and which one should gate a page for what.

title: Database Indexing for Time-Series: B-Tree vs BRIN in PostgreSQL
summary: Why a Block Range Index, not the default B-Tree, is the right structure for naturally time-ordered data — and why QuantAlpha's tick-ingestion pipeline hasn't needed it yet.

title: Gossip Protocol Visualizer: How Cluster Membership Actually Spreads
summary: A real push-based epidemic broadcast, run and scrubbed round by round, showing why gossip converges in O(log n) rounds instead of O(n).

title: Rate Limiting Algorithms: Token Bucket vs Leaky Bucket vs Fixed Window
summary: Three rate limiting algorithms, run for real against the same burst scenario, to show what each one actually does differently — not just what it's named.

title: WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events: What Holding 5,000 Connections Open Actually Costs
summary: A real harness measuring server memory for thousands of concurrent WebSocket vs SSE connections — written before the article, per the lesson from three prior benchmark rewrites.

title: Designing a Global API Gateway: Edge Routing Beyond a Single Aegis Instance
summary: Aegis's GraphQL gateway solves API shape for one instance. This is the layer above it a real deployment would need once there's more than one — and why that's a different problem, not a bigger version of the same one.

title: The SPA Google Never Saw

title: ADR: Why Prerender Instead of Migrating to Next.js
summary: This portfolio's original decision to build a custom JAMstack instead of using Next.js still held once a crawler-visibility bug surfaced. Here's why the fix was a build step, not a framework migration.

title: Field Note: A Diagram That Wouldn't Render
summary: A sequence diagram in a new case study failed to parse. The cause wasn't the character I suspected first — and the fix I tried second broke the same way for a different reason.

title: Field Note: Measuring Contrast Instead of Guessing at It
summary: A prior audit flagged 44 text-slate-400 occurrences as 'potentially borderline' and correctly refused to fix them blind. Building a real contrast checker turned that judgment call into a number — and found two unrelated bugs on the way.

summary: A working engineer's honest comparison of Go and TypeScript for backend services, based on using both in production — and a framework for choosing between them.

summary: An interactive benchmark comparing the time it takes to replay tens of thousands of immutable events into a Read Projection.
